top_choice_rationale: P001 (Adonis alone) remains my first choice on literary grounds. The case is formal and linguistic: Songs of Mihyar the Damascene and A Time Between Ashes and Roses, as publicly described, renew the idiom of Arabic verse through myth and fragmentation while arguing with the classical tradition. The oeuvre is long and fully formed, so it can be judged as a whole now. I would anchor the citation in the poetry and name the poetics only as the thing that informs it, so critical influence is not a second ground for the award. The main limits are that the prosodic and allusive core is what translation transmits least well, and that my reading rests on translations and secondary accounts. I also cannot show from the supplied record whether the later decades, including Al-Kitab, deepen the project or repeat it. The recommendation should state this reliance openly and invite a reader of Arabic to test the claims. P002 (Cărtărescu) is a close second and would be my choice if the Arabic evidence cannot be made firm. His large prose architecture is easier to assess under uncertainty, but his late volumes face the same test as Adonis's later decades. P003 (Carson) is a serious case, but I cannot yet establish its breadth beyond the best-known works. Book-object forms and the concentration of her reception also make it harder to judge. P000 is last. Translation limits apply to every candidate and do not justify withholding the prize when the central works can be argued on literary grounds.
recusal_note: None apparent from the profile. I have no documented connection to Adonis, Cărtărescu, Carson or any other shortlisted writer. For transparency, I was elected alongside Steve Sem-Sandberg in 2020 and work with chair Anders Olsson. I am married to Pär Nuder, and as Permanent Secretary I am expected to announce the laureate. None of these relates to a shortlisted writer. I am one of three explicit supporters of P001, and my committee voting status is undocumented, so my simulated vote is a modeling assumption. Conflicts are disclosed here and not adjudicated.
